stem: A 28-year-old mover picks up first a pencil and then a heavy box using the same arm muscles. The greater force needed for the box is generated mainly by which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Widening of the zone of filament overlap
options.misconception: The length-tension relationship is being cast as the grading mechanism.
options.explanation: Overlap affects the force each fiber can produce at a given length, but voluntary force grading in a working muscle comes from recruiting additional motor units.

options.label: B
options.text: Shortening of every sarcomere by a greater distance
options.misconception: A bigger per-sarcomere stroke is being cast as the grading mechanism.
options.explanation: Each sarcomere shortens to an anatomical limit set by filament overlap; whole-muscle force is graded by how many motor units participate, not by extra sarcomere travel.

options.label: C
options.text: Fusion of twitches into a continuous contraction
options.misconception: Temporal summation is being cast as the main grading mechanism here.
options.explanation: Tetanus (fused twitches) raises tension within an active unit, but picking up a heavier load engages MORE motor units through recruitment.

options.label: D
options.text: Conversion of slow fibers into fast fibers
options.misconception: A training adaptation is being cast as an acute force mechanism.
options.explanation: Fiber-type conversion is a slow adaptation to training; it cannot supply extra force within the seconds it takes to lift a box.

options.label: E
options.text: Recruitment of larger, higher-threshold motor units
options.misconception: None; force is graded by calling in bigger motor units.
options.explanation: Small, low-threshold motor units fire first; as more strength is needed, larger motor units with higher-threshold neurons are enlisted, and this recruitment makes the contraction progressively stronger.

context: Learning objective: the size principle. A motor unit = one motor neuron plus all its fibers. Small, low-threshold units fire first for delicate force; larger, higher-threshold units are recruited as demand rises (the largest can produce 50x the tension of the smallest). Recruitment grades whole-muscle force.
